judge.access: in-session judgement by the build worker (Claude Code); no API call

mathlib.validation: imported-build: the pinned mathlib cache (lake exe cache get) was imported; no local re-check of proofs

nlab.reuse: Using and distributing content obtained from the nLab is free and encouraged if you acknowledge the source, as usual in academia. (nLab HomePage)

wikidata.access: MediaWiki Action API, no account, one request per second, descriptive User-Agent
wikidata.version: per item: the item's last revision ID (lastrevid) at retrieval
wikidata.reuse: Wikidata structured data is CC0. Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0: the catalog quotes at most the first two sentences of a lead section, with its title, revision and link (https://foundation.wikimedia.org/wiki/Policy:Terms_of_Use).

wikipedia.access: MediaWiki Action API, no account, one request per second, descriptive User-Agent
wikipedia.version: per page: the revision ID at retrieval
wikipedia.reuse: Wikidata structured data is CC0. Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0: the catalog quotes at most the first two sentences of a lead section, with its title, revision and link (https://foundation.wikimedia.org/wiki/Policy:Terms_of_Use).

theoremsearch.license: cc-by-4.0 (dataset card); each paper row also keeps its own license field
theoremsearch.scope: the public dataset at the pinned revision; not the live TheoremSearch service, whose coverage differs
theoremsearch.reuse: CC BY 4.0 (dataset card): attribute uw-math-ai/theorem-search-dataset-permissive; passages keep their arXiv paper ID and the paper row's own license

taxonomy.reuse: arXiv category names and descriptions, quoted as facts of the classification for attribution.

concepts.reuse: nLab Idea passages are quoted with acknowledgement (nLab terms); Mathlib doc comments are Apache-2.0; judge text is authored for this catalog.

scale.u: unknown: no evidence supports a score
scale.na: not applicable: the component does not apply to this result
scale.odd: Scores 1 and 3 are intermediate judgments between the adjacent anchors.

components.name: Effectiveness
components.question: How fully does the result achieve the stated goals?

anchors.0: No contribution to the specified goal

components.name: Research influence
components.question: Which later results and research questions does the evidence connect to it?

anchors.0: Evidence establishes no contribution within the evaluated scope
anchors.2: Enables identifiable later results or questions
anchors.4: Sources establish substantial influence on research directions

components.name: Practical impact
components.question: Which documented applications and consequences does it support?

anchors.0: Evidence establishes no useful contribution in the evaluated cases
anchors.4: Supports substantial consequences across documented applications

components.name: Reach
components.question: Across which problems, fields, and levels does it provide value?

anchors.0: No applicable case within the declared scope
anchors.2: Applies to several cases within one area
anchors.4: Sources establish broad use across distinct areas and levels

components.name: Low hypothesis burden
components.question: How broadly do its conditions permit use?

anchors.0: Conditions exclude almost all declared cases
anchors.4: Conditions permit almost all declared cases

components.name: Proof simplicity
components.question: How much conceptual machinery does the selected proof require?

anchors.0: Extensive specialized machinery in the selected proof
anchors.4: Few elementary concepts and direct steps

components.name: Application simplicity
components.question: How much effort does a stated application require?

anchors.0: Extensive extra inputs, machinery, or adaptation
anchors.4: Direct use with few inputs and steps

rubric.aggregate: overall = sum(w_i * r_i / 4) over the 7 components, with weights that sum to 100. If a component is u or na, the overall score is unknown; the page shows the interval with 0 and 4 put in for each missing component.

case_set.rule: For a catalog result, the generated case set is the goal that its own statement names (the conclusion under its hypotheses) plus the goals of the documented uses in its evidence. Effectiveness is judged against these goals; comparison cases (cases.json) add fixed goals with calculated guarantees.
case_set.warning: Case coverage differs between results. The global score is an experimental summary, not a universal benchmark.

confidence.high: statement complete in a source, several independent sources, scores consistent with the second assessment where one ran
confidence.medium: statement complete, evidence from one or two sources, or a second assessment differs by 1 on some components
confidence.low: thin evidence (one passage or a formal record only), or a second assessment differs by 2 or more
confidence.note: Labels describe evidence completeness and assessment consistency. They are not probabilities.

concept_rubric.about: The rubric of the concept catalog. It mirrors te-rubric/1: seven components scored 0 to 4 (u unknown, na not applicable), weights that sum to 100, the same aggregate and the same confidence labels. Four components ask the result rubric's questions of a concept; three replace the proof and application components, which do not apply to a definition.

scale.u: unknown: no evidence supports a score
scale.na: not applicable: the component does not apply to this concept
scale.odd: Scores 1 and 3 are intermediate judgments between the adjacent anchors.

components.name: Unifying power
components.question: How many distinct examples, phenomena and results does the one definition organize?

anchors.0: Organizes no recognised family of examples or results
anchors.2: Organizes the examples and results of one area
anchors.4: A central organizing notion across many areas

components.name: Research influence
components.question: Which research directions and later results does the evidence connect to the concept?

anchors.0: Evidence establishes no research use within the evaluated scope
anchors.2: Underlies identifiable results or questions in one area
anchors.4: Sources establish substantial influence on research directions

components.name: Practical impact
components.question: Which documented uses outside pure mathematics (science, engineering, computing, statistics, finance) does it support?

anchors.0: No documented use outside pure mathematics
anchors.2: Supports documented uses in one applied field
anchors.4: Supports substantial uses across applied fields

components.name: Reach
components.question: Across which problems, fields and levels does it appear?

anchors.0: Appears only in its own narrow topic
anchors.2: Appears across several topics of one area
anchors.4: Sources establish use across distinct areas and levels

components.name: Low prerequisite burden
components.question: How little prior machinery does the definition need?

anchors.0: The definition needs extensive specialized machinery
anchors.2: The definition needs several substantial prior concepts
anchors.4: The definition needs only elementary notions

components.name: Example accessibility
components.question: How readily do concrete examples and non-examples build intuition?

anchors.2: Standard examples need some work to verify

components.name: Computability
components.question: How directly can a reader compute or check an instance?

anchors.0: Instances are rarely computable or checkable
anchors.2: Computable in standard cases by a multi-step procedure

concept_rubric.aggregate: overall = sum(w_i * r_i / 4) over the 7 components, with weights that sum to 100. If a component with a weight above 0 is unknown or not applicable, the aggregate is unknown and the interval puts 0 and 4 in for it.
concept_rubric.depths: understand: state the definition and recognise examples; apply: compute with the concept and use it in problems; prove: prove its standard properties and work with it in proofs. Effort bands as te-learn/1: 1 under 1 hour, 2 hours, 3 days, 4 weeks, 5 months, for a reader at the concept's needed level.

confidence.high: the concept has a formal definition in a source (mathlib or nLab), several results name it, and the scores follow from that evidence
confidence.medium: a source defines it, or several results name it, but not both
confidence.low: thin evidence: the judge's own knowledge with at most one source record
confidence.note: Labels describe evidence completeness. They are not probabilities.
